clue.text: Wordsmiths rephrase logic mistakenly incorporating unknown

indicators.note: the jumbled letters take in the unknown, holding it within them
something done mistakenly is jumbled, so the letters of the two words before it are rearranged

parts.note: X is the classic algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Someone tells a clumsy writer to rephrase their muddled logic, as wordsmiths would.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mistakenly' rearranges REPHRASE LOGIC into LEICOGRAPHERS; 'incorporating' puts X inside, after the opening LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Dictionary compilers are people whose craft is words, so wordsmiths is a playful description of them.

clue.text: Administration putting writer in place

indicators.note: the writer is put in, so it sits inside the word for place

parts.note: a locality is a place or district
an author is a writer

explanation.surface: A government body appoints a writer to a post somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' signals insertion: the writer splits the word for place after its fifth letter, and the two halves read as a phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: A council that runs a town or county is a body of local government, an administration.

clue.text: Special quality of vote for accepting parliamentary bill

parts.note: a cross, X, is the mark made on a ballot paper

indicators.note: the word for takes in the bill, holding it inside

parts.note: taken as written
a bill passed by Parliament becomes an Act

explanation.surface: A voter backs a parliamentary bill for some special quality it has.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names an indefinable star quality, popularised by a TV talent show of that name.

clue.text: Thrilling end to episode with French flag flying across Italy

indicators.note: the jumbled letters stretch across the letter for Italy, enclosing it
a flag flying flaps about, so the letters of the two words before it are tossed into a new order

parts.note: I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: An episode ends dramatically with the French tricolour flown across Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flying' rearranges FRENCH FLAG into CLFFHANGER; 'across' puts I inside it, after CL.
explanation.definitionFit: A suspenseful ending that leaves the audience in suspense until the next instalment is exactly this kind of finish.

clue.text: High-ranking people should change sides in a mild way

indicators.note: right becomes left: the R in the word for the high-ranking people is swapped for L

parts.note: the gentry are the people of good social standing

explanation.surface: A moral that the upper classes ought to switch allegiance, but gently.
explanation.walkthrough: Changing sides swaps R (right) for L (left) in GENTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something softly and without force is to do it in a mild manner, an adverb for adverb.

clue.text: Noticed changes after answer is put into effect

indicators.note: the rearranged letters come after the abbreviation
the word noticed changes its form, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone noticed changes after an answer was implemented.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' is the anagram signal, not a noun; 'after' places the rearrangement behind the single letter, and 'is' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Office jargon: a request that has been actioned has been carried out, dealt with in practice.

clue.text: House intermittently providing shade

indicators.note: taking letters on and off, so only the first, third and fifth letters of house are kept

explanation.surface: A building that only sometimes gives shelter from the sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A colour or tint is called a shade, and the two words are close synonyms.

clue.text: Wild sheep sound out of breath

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep
to pant is to breathe in short gasps

explanation.surface: A wild sheep gasping for air.
explanation.definitionFit: Unchecked and running wild, as rampant weeds or rampant inflation, matching wild in its unrestrained sense.

clue.text: Material for cast seeing opera stars flip out

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of their order, so the three words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: An opera singer breaks a leg on stage after the stars flip out, and needs a cast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flip' looks like part of the indicator ('flip out'), but it is fodder: its letters are needed in the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A white gypsum powder that sets hard when mixed with water, traditionally used for setting broken limbs.

clue.text: Clear sort of call from family touring port

indicators.note: the family goes round the port, enclosing it

parts.note: a clan is an extended family, especially in Scotland
Rio de Janeiro, a Brazilian port, is often called simply Rio

explanation.surface: A family on tour sounds a loud summons from the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: A clarion was a shrill trumpet, so a clarion call is a loud, clear rallying cry.

clue.text: Short story about the girl's millions is hot air

indicators.note: the shortened story goes about the pronoun and abbreviation, enclosing them
short means cut off, so the last letter of the word for story is dropped

parts.note: a tale is a story
her is the possessive for a girl
M is the abbreviation for million

explanation.surface: A tale of some girl's fortune that is nothing but bluster.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' cuts the last letter from the story, and 'about' wraps what is left round the rest. 'Hot air' sounds like idle talk, but here it is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: A rising current of warm air, used by gliders and birds to gain height.

clue.text: Mostly reluctant crowd …

indicators.note: mostly means most but not all, so the last letter is dropped

parts.note: loth is an old spelling of loath, meaning reluctant

explanation.surface: A largely unwilling throng, leading via the ellipsis into the next clue.
explanation.definitionFit: A group or set of people, as in 'that lot over there', so a gathering or crowd.

clue.text: … packed with runners in high spirits

parts.note: full of means crammed with
runner beans are a common garden vegetable, so runners are beans

explanation.surface: Continuing the ellipsis: a crowd crammed with athletes, all buoyant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'runners' suggests athletes, but it is the runner bean, a climbing vegetable grown in British gardens.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for being lively and energetic, bursting with cheerful vitality.

clue.text: Brewing artisan beer is a difficult exercise

indicators.note: brewing turns ingredients into something new, so the letters of the two words after it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Making craft beer at home turns out to be hard work.
explanation.definitionFit: A puzzle that taxes the mind is a tough mental workout, a difficult exercise for the intellect.

clue.text: Angry protest and row coming after universal voting system

indicators.note: the word for row is placed after the letters for universal and the voting system

parts.note: U is the film certificate for universal viewing
PR is proportional representation, an electoral system
an oar is what you row with

explanation.surface: A noisy row erupts over the introduction of a universal voting system.
explanation.definitionFit: A loud public outcry or commotion of complaint, so a furious protest.

clue.text: Theatrical skill needing repeated energy and banter?

parts.note: rep is short for repertory theatre
art is a skill or knack

indicators.note: the energy letter is given twice

parts.note: E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A performer's craft needs plenty of energy and a gift for witty back-and-forth.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick witty exchange of remarks and retorts is good-humoured teasing talk, which is banter.

clue.text: Skater must fail in the Caribbean islands, and try another sport

indicators.note: the jumbled letters go in the abbreviation for the islands

parts.note: WI stands for the West Indies

indicators.note: the skater falls in a heap, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A skater who keeps failing in the Caribbean switches to a different sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'must fail' is the anagram signal; 'in' puts the jumble between the two letters for the West Indies. The definition is a verb phrase, matching the hyphenated verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To glide over water on skis towed by a boat is to take up a different sport, here as a verb.

clue.text: Try protecting distressed aged bowler, perhaps

indicators.note: the word for try surrounds the jumbled letters, protecting them

parts.note: a judge will hear, or try, a case

indicators.note: distressed means knocked about, so the letters of aged are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tired old cricket bowler needs a helmet for protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bowler' suggests cricket, but it is the hard round hat. 'Try' is the legal sense: a judge tries, or hears, a case.
explanation.definitionFit: A bowler is a hard felt hat, one example of something worn on the head.

clue.text: Notice caller dismissing Italian consultant

parts.note: an ad is a notice, an advertisement

indicators.note: dismissing sends away the abbreviation for Italian from the word for caller

parts.note: a visitor is someone who calls
It is short for Italian, as in It vermouth

explanation.surface: A caller tells an Italian to leave, then calls in an expert.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who gives professional advice is a consultant; the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: Popular detective needing match for dye

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
DI is a Detective Inspector
to go is to match or suit, as colours go together

explanation.surface: A well-loved detective seeks a colour match for a dye.
explanation.definitionFit: A deep blue dye, originally from a plant, so a dye by its name.

clue.text: Using time on the inside, beat urge

indicators.note: only the inner letters of time are taken, dropping its first and last

parts.note: a pulse is a beat, as of the heart

explanation.surface: A prisoner using time inside to beat an urge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the inside' suggests prison but means the middle letters of 'time', IM.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden desire to act, without thought, is the same thing as an urge.

clue.text: Heart monitor's first indicator

indicators.note: only the opening letter of monitor's is taken

parts.note: an arrow is a pointer or indicator

explanation.surface: A hospital monitor's first sign of the heart's condition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart' and 'monitor' suggest a cardiac machine, but heart means the core of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The inner core or essence of something, as in being chilled to the marrow, is its heart.

clue.text: Right — always represent value and ring

parts.note: ever means always, as in ever hopeful
to be is to represent, as an actor is the king
to rate is to value

explanation.surface: Right, always stand for value and integrity: a slogan with a ring to it.
explanation.definitionFit: To echo and resound is to ring out, as a bell's sound carries.

clue.text: Music from 'American Dad'!

definitions.meaning: chart music aimed at a wide audience
in the US a father is familiarly called by this short word

explanation.surface: A song from the cartoon show American Dad!
explanation.walkthrough: The clue borrows the title of an American cartoon series, but the words are a plain description of a father in the US.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for popular music, and also an American familiar word for a father.

clue.text: Experiences no end of alarm in upsetting smart set

indicators.note: upsetting knocks things over, so the remaining letters are rearranged
no letter of that kind is left in, so it is removed from the phrase smart set
no letter of that kind is left in, so it is removed from the phrase smart set
the final letter of alarm is the one taken

explanation.surface: Fashionable society people are upset, and alarm has no end.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of 'alarm' is M; take it from SMART SET and 'upsetting' rearranges SARTSET.
explanation.definitionFit: A taster is a small sample, so tasters are brief experiences of something.

clue.text: Feel foolish boxing leprechaun?

indicators.note: the two words hold the answer boxed up inside them, across the gap

explanation.surface: Someone feels foolish after taking on a leprechaun in a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A leprechaun is an Irish fairy, an example of a small mischievous sprite, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Thief may be good person protected by sovereign

indicators.note: the saint sits inside the word for sovereign, sheltered by it

parts.note: a ruler is a sovereign monarch
ST is a saint, a good person

explanation.surface: A thief might be a decent sort shielded by the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sovereign' could be the gold coin, but here it is the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A livestock stealer, especially of cattle or horses, is a particular kind of thief.

clue.text: Run campaigns including study for penalising people

parts.note: to run goods is to smuggle or traffic in them

indicators.note: the word for campaigns includes the study within it

parts.note: military campaigns are wars
a den is a private room, a study

explanation.surface: Organising campaigns that include study, for those who issue penalties.
explanation.walkthrough: TRAFFIC WARDENS are the British officials who issue parking tickets.
explanation.definitionFit: Parking officials who issue fines to drivers are people whose job is penalising motorists.
